steps: Identify the normal force N exerted by the wall, which equals the pressing force: N = 100 N.
Calculate the maximum static frictional force: f_max = \mu N = 0.3 \times 100 = 30 N.
Calculate the downward force due to gravity (weight) assuming g = 10 m/s^2: W = mg = 2 \times 10 = 20 N.
Compare W and f_max: since 20 N \le 30 N, the body does not slide and is in static equilibrium.
In static equilibrium, the actual frictional force adjusts to equal the applied downward force: f = W = 20 N.
